metadata.title: Developing the Teacher mentoring self-efficacy scale (TMSES) using the Delphi method and exploratory factor analysis

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This study does not use an ILSA micro-dataset (e.g., PISA/TALIS) for student achievement scaling; instead, it develops and validates a new teacher-mentor self-efficacy instrument (TMSES) using a UK-based Delphi panel and an online survey of teacher mentors. Because the analysis is based on psychometric scale development (Delphi consensus and exploratory factor analysis) rather than a complex survey of students, there is no international sampling design requiring student-level survey weights or replicate-weight variance estimation. The authors report using complete responses only for the exploratory factor analysis (N=239) to avoid statistical issues from missing data, rather than applying PV-based scaling or survey-weighted estimation. Consequently, no PV handling or ILSA-style weighting variables (e.g., TOTWGT/W_FSTUWT) are applicable to the reported analyses.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values (PVs) are generated for cognitive achievement domains in ILSA assessments (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/TALIS achievement scales). Here, the dependent variables are Likert-scale self-efficacy items used for scale construction and exploratory factor analysis, not PV-based achievement scores. Therefore, PV handling is not applicable by design, and the paper instead focuses on psychometric item structure and reliability.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Phase 1 Delphi: 74 individuals contacted; 31 accepted; 5 withdrew; final panel size 26 UK-based experts (minimum 5 years experience). Phase 2 survey: 297 respondents started the survey; only fully completed surveys were used for exploratory factor analysis to avoid statistical issues from missing data, yielding N=239. The survey was open to anyone with experience of teacher mentoring across the whole sector, but nearly all respondents were based in the UK (99.2%).

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict Literature synthesis outcome (not student-level prediction), finding that This paper develops the Teacher Mentoring Self-Efficacy Scale (TMSES) through a two-phase mixed-methods design: a UK-based three-round Delphi study (N=26 experts) to generate 44 mentoring competencies, followed by a UK-based online survey of teacher mentors (N=239 fully completed responses) to test the underlying scale structure. The quantitative phase uses exploratory factor analysis with principal axis factoring and direct oblimin rotation, after checking normality, Bartlett’s test of sphericity, and KMO (KMO=0.954). The final solution is a 16-item two-factor model accounting for 61.07% of total variance, with strong loadings (e.g., item 1 loading=0.96; item 29 loading=0.83). Reliability is high (Cronbach’s alpha: total scale α=0.94; factor alphas α=0.94 and α=0.84). Because this is psychometric scale development (not predictive ML on ILSA achievement PVs), there are no ML performance metrics, no survey-weighted estimation, and no PV handling; generalizability is limited by UK-only and COVID-19-era data collection. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This is not an empirical predictive ML study using ILSA microdata; it is a psychometric instrument development paper using Delphi consensus and exploratory factor analysis. As a result, there are no ILSA program/cycle/domain datasets, no PV-based achievement outcomes, no ML algorithms, and no predictive performance metrics to extract. The main quantitative outputs are factor structure (variance explained, loadings) and reliability (Cronbach’s alpha), which are outside the ML schema.
